title: Moment of Revelation
subtitle: Paris is a dream unto itself, and that dream is ending.

trails.title: Witness Report
trails.description: An unremarkable witness report. All rumors, whispers, and tales—every passerby keeps a few in their pockets.

content.text: A painter sketching in a square remembers reaching a point where his artwork was "stuck in a bottleneck." That's when a "young person with a uniquely inspired touch" helped him finish it. The piece, with its "exquisite cubist composition," now "shines with the light of a new-age Muse." The painter believes this must be the work of "some magnificent god of art" who manifested to guide him.

items.text: She runs through the endless white, not knowing what she's searching for, nor where the path will end.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Streams of fate ... But how can I find them? Dowsing might be a little on the nose.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Damn! She was just steps away from me when I was in the car!
Her steps grow heavy, but she doesn't stop, until "Paris" appears before her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wh-What's that?
A city pierces the clouds, mirrored in the sky. People and beasts alike stop to stare up at the mirrored double above her.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: How spectacular! If this isn't a miracle, then I must ask what else could possibly qualify as one?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Let dusty historians scoff and rivals sneer! But there are none who would dare scorn this timeless, flawless vision of Parisian beauty across the ages!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Who from this lofty perch would deny this is the truest form of Paris?

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: The Palace of Optics, the Eiffel Tower, the Arc de Triomphe, Notre-Dame, the Luxor Obelisk, the Lutetia Arena, the medieval quarters—each piece woven together in perfect harmony!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: As I've said, thought shapes reality. This Paris—born from collective imagination—is Paris at its most true and most real!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Only when it fully descends shall we finally possess a real world—a life worth living!
One embraces the sky. One holds the key to the ritual. The last remains silent.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Must you hang over me like this, Roseau?

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: And you, madame, did you foresee this?

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: The fate of Paris now rests in my hands, and yet I remain myself. What a pity it must be for you.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Hmph, no more tricks?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: "What lies below shall reflect what lies above"? So, this is what will befall Paris?
She reaches toward Félicienne, but her hand passes straight through her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I can't touch her.
She tries everything—attacking, casting arcane skills, pinching her own arm—until a flash of white swallows her entirely.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You have returned.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What?!
When she blinks, she's back inside the taxi.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: H-How am I back in here?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You failed to take back your body. So long as you return here, though, there is still a chance.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I found Félicienne! She—I was right next to her, but I couldn't reach her no matter how I tried!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Then give up, and accept this as your final resting place.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No, I won't sit here and do nothing. I will destroy that diamond. I must, for Célia.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But how am I supposed to reach Félicienne?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Wait. I don't really need to reach her, do I?
She snaps upright, remembering.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Madame Bouanich, you said before that the stream of my fate merged with Félicienne's.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So, in a sense, she and I are always together, right?
Her fingers brush the dragon's spine in her pocket—the smooth cut, the limp tail tip.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Then I don't need to "find her" nor even "find myself." Because she is me, and I am her!

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You have begun to understand.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: She only had the means to claim your body because your spirits are closely intertwined.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Any impact to your body affects both souls. Though the weaker of the two spirits often cannot endure the strain.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: "Often," but not never, no? So even you can't see what comes next.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You don't know whether Félicienne or I will win this fight!
She locks eyes with the impartial diviner. And then she sees it—the flaw, the crack in the illusion.
Beryl meets her gaze. For once, real fire flickers in those crystalline eyes.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: The currents of fate will bend to your actions. You will steer its course rather than be swept away.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You have never once yielded before destiny, and that is precisely why I have followed you from the beginning.
She no longer looks detached and polished, no longer like a crystal reflecting every light but her own.
The diviner finally descends to the world as it is.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: It is as you say. I do not know if you'll emerge victorious in this final trial.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: Will you carry this through for me?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Do you even need to ask?
The fragments in her hand pulse in time with her heartbeat.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So, Félicienne. Time for you to experience the Tavernier family curse.
Her marvelous little dragon pokes its head from her pocket, sparks flaring from its nostrils.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: If our fates are truly entwined, then this curse must bind your soul as well as mine. And in true Tavernier fashion, your end will come just as you lay hands on the treasure you desire most.
The ritual proceeds moment by moment as the Paris above them begins drawing closer to the ground, the twin Eiffel Towers nearing collision.
Unnatural light emits brightly from the diamond, drawing the two worlds together.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Incredible, Félicienne! Just a little longer, and Paris, as it should be, born from the collective unconscious, will descend into reality!

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: The true Paris—not like the garbage heap below us!
*bang*
A bullet grazes the diamond. Félicienne instinctively shields it with her hand. The mirrored city above begins to fade.
Eiffel Tower, Paris

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Célia? How did you get here? How are you still alive?
The professor's assistant stands with a gun aimed at him, but her outline wavers, ghost-like, just like the reflection above them.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Adèle called out to me.

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: Fascinating. Truly fascinating! Your soul should've been erased by Félicienne. I must thank you once again, my most brilliant student. Your existence confirms another of my theories:

items.speaker: Professor Roseau
items.text: The Depths of Myth promises more than just resurrection, but an end to death itself!

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Heh, a friend of Adèle's? No doubt you're as tactless as she was.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: You intend to stop me? Be my guest.
She lifts the diamond to her chest, right before her heart.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Go on. You should be grateful I've given you the opportunity.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Whether you hit me or the diamond, you'll stop the ritual. Go on.

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: You really think threatening Adèle's body will intimidate me? It won't work.
Her hand trembles. She fears missing the shot or, worse, hitting true.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Yet, is that hesitation I see? Think about what our dear Adèle would say at a time like this—"pull the trigger." Sounds like her, doesn't it?

items.speaker: Célia
items.text: Shut up! Shut up!

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: My, my, have I said something wrong? Or perhaps you don't know Adèle as well as you thought.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Here, let me show you in a more vivid manner.
The woman inhabiting Adèle's body tilts her head with one hand, as if shaking loose her thoughts.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: Don't worry about me. Just shoot. Take us both out. It's what you have to do.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: It's the only way to break my family curse. You have to end the adventure with my death.

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: To fall at the height of a brilliant journey. That's better than fading into some bleak, ordinary end, no?

items.speaker: "Félicienne"
items.text: No, Célia. You don't need to do this! I'll end this myself.

items.speaker: "Félicienne" & Célia
items.text: Huh?!
An unexpected line is delivered in the clumsy play, stunning both the actress and her audience.
And at that moment, the sleeping dragon awakens in her pocket.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Aaagghh!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: You irritating little lizard, how dare you harm your own master?!

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Damn you, Adèle! You and your wretched pet!
Flame sears through the haze, pain burning away the chaos of her memory.
The scorching heat, purging all illusion, returns the body to its rightful owner, finally allowing her to move freely.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: So this is what it feels like for a soul to be scorched. I finally understand why so many fear hell.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Adèle, you fool! Tell your pet to stop at once! Do you wish to die with me?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No, I don't. Not right now, Félicienne. So why don't you drop the diamond?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: I can already guess your response.

items.speaker: Adèle & Félicienne
items.text: You keep dreaming! This diamond belongs to me! Not even death can steal it from me!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Heh, listen to you. You'd make an excellent Tavernier.
Félicienne's anger only grows, her left hand clutching the diamond tighter still as the flames crawl further up her body inch by inch.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Now let's see if fire can separate true from false, Félicienne!
